title: Her rooms on E deck (the upper deck): R3 pilot, a sourced table of facts
written: 2026-11-20, by the R3 pilot session (Claude Opus 5.5), under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md
rules: Facts only: which room, where, how big, which door to which. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites the reference read and the original checked, or says it was not checked. Bets are tagged as bets.
reference: ET: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, E deck (https://www.encyclopedia-titanica.org/titanic-deckplans/e-deck.html; drawn by Bruce Beveridge for Titanic The Ship Magnificent, The History Press 2008), read on the page in the built-in browser on 2026-11-20, nothing saved
original: Shipbuilder 1911: The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 (the Olympic and Titanic number), plate 4d, 'Upper Deck E', as reproduced by GG Archives (https://www.ggarchives.com/OT/Titanic/25-ImageLibrary/TheShipbuilder-10-Design-SpecialPlates.html); the largest copy there is 1000 x 129 px, so only its big labels and blocks can be read. It shows the class as designed in 1911.
how: x: walls by her frames, read off the frame numbers the reference prints every second frame along the centreline; a frame's place is its tick, measured on the page with a ruler in the page (no image kept).

Frames to feet: the reference's own scale, set by her 36 in frames amidships (30.75 px a frame on the page, 0.09756 ft a pixel), from the midship section between frames 1A and 1F. At that scale the stem at E deck falls 425.3 ft forward of amidships (the model's FP is 425.0 ft).

y: feet from the centreline, port positive, at 0.0981 ft a pixel (the reference's breadth over the shell amidships is 944 px for 92.67 ft). 'shell+' and 'shell-' are her side; in metres the tool puts it at the model's half-breadth at mid-height between E and D decks [stand-in for the reference's shell].
Walls marked 'ruler' were measured on the page to a pixel (1.2 in); the rest are read by eye, to about a frame and a foot, and are tagged 'approx'.

Doors: the width is the reference's where it writes one; otherwise 2 ft 3 in, the default [bet: the door arcs on the reference measure 2 ft 2 in to 2 ft 6 in]. Watertight doors: 3 ft [bet; not written on the reference].
Dense cabins are blocks: one row for the cabins between two passages, with the cabin numbers listed (tag 'block').
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, poly_m, area_m2, zone, slab, plan_compartment) are written by: node tools/rooms_table.js --write data/rooms/E_deck.json

frames.note: Her frames as the reference draws them: [frame, feet forward of amidships]. Interpolated linearly between anchors. Frame numbers run from amidships both ways (1A and 1F have the midship section between them). Drawn spacing: 36 in from about 108A to about 90F; closing to about 24 in at the bow and about 27 in at the stern.

bulkheads.note: Watertight bulkheads where the reference marks them on E deck (W.T.B. labels, or W.T.D. doors in a line). C to J stop under E deck and are not drawn on it.

side.note: Read 2026-11-20 between 22:50 and 23:02 CST, both sides, with the line test. E deck ends at the AP (148A): there its two sides meet. For BACKLOG G14 (the hull's ends): tools/rooms_table_tests.js sets each against the model's half-breadth. Frames 75A to 40A and 40F to 75F added 2026-11-21 between 05:20 and 05:45 CST by the B1+B2 lane, the same method in the built-in browser (nothing saved), for C3 (the epoch's hull ends, D80; G20's G14 half): every 5 frames, no reading off the smooth line through its neighbours by more than 0.1 m, so no single frames were added. At R3's 80A and 80F on C and D decks, and at 80F and 80A on E, the same reading gives R3's figures within 0.1 ft (one pixel).
side.unit: ft from the centreline to her outer line as the plan draws it, port and starboard, read on the page at 1:1 by pixel profile: from her outside inward, the first dark pixel that lies on a continuous line (a dark path running at least 28 px each way along her), at three columns 6 px apart about the frame's tick; the median of the three. Annotations outside her (labels, dimension arrows) fail the line test. null: no reading (the line broken there by fittings).
